assessment: The incumbent provides a reversible assembled product, an order-slip check and layout guidance, but reported partition errors and observed customer confusion indicate incomplete protection. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, limiting any claim that full assembly inherently prevents the eight-minute target (D2-O6). Mixed batches contained every extreme delay, but layout complexity and switching are confounded. Overlapping widths among successful and repeated insertions also limit a width-only explanation (D2-O5). Reported errors are not an audited completeness rate; combined timing and the ten-person session cannot establish pilot success.

openings.claim: Order changes may increase selection and checking time or mistakes; an order-specific parts staging card could improve the incumbent without changing assembled delivery.
openings.delta: Separate switching overhead from layout complexity, then test a count-and-shape checklist with a verified exterior-color field.
openings.prediction: With identical layout composition, alternating orders will take longer than grouped orders, principally during selection/checking; staging will reduce that difference and observed content errors.
openings.probe: Reuse six spare-board samples across paired grouped/alternating sequences for both workers, counterbalancing sequence order. Record selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, plus independently checked contents. Compare current picking with staging. Admit changes only within cost caps and available time before the fixed delivery date.
assumptions: Practice and complexity can be balanced; batch association alone is not causal.

openings.claim: Does an order-specific diagram resolve short-partition confusion when supplied components are verified correct?
openings.delta: Distinguish interpretation difficulty from missing parts and insertion difficulty.
openings.prediction: If interpretation is limiting, the tailored diagram will reduce wrong-location attempts and help requests while insertion retries at correctly identified slots persist.
openings.probe: Assign five participants to each diagram, using verified matched kits and recording first location choice, insertion retries, assistance and completion time. Reuse samples. Treat this as screening; verify final pilot thresholds separately before claiming success.
assumptions: Diagrams replace existing guidance within both cost caps.
Components, rearrangeability, ordered colors/counts, footprint, capacity and delivery date remain as stipulated.
